mainTopic: שבועת העדות: what counts as a demand, why only a denial in בית דין counts, witnesses denying together or one after another, and the single witness and דבר הגורם לממון
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of שמואל's rule. If a plaintiff only runs after witnesses and they swear on their own that they know no testimony, they are פטור. The גמרא shows that the משנה's word 'said' is not strict, because people usually make their demands out loud. A ברייתא then supports שמואל. Next, אביי learns from 'אם לוא יגיד' that only a denial in בית דין makes witnesses liable, since only there would their testimony make someone pay. From רב פפא's challenge, the גמרא concludes that the oath can be taken outside בית דין but the denial must be in בית דין. For two witnesses who deny 'together', רב חסדא says the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. רבי יוחנן instead explains it with תוך כדי דיבור. Finally, the גמרא explains why the second witness is exempt, which brings in the argument about a single witness and דבר הגורם לממון. It then starts explaining אביי's list of סוטה witness cases, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Witnesses must hear the demand from the plaintiff
steps.stepSummary: The end of the גמרא's challenge: we already learned that witnesses are only liable when they hear the demand from the plaintiff's own mouth, so what does שמואל add?
steps.simpleTranslation: …until they hear it from the mouth of the plaintiff! So why did שמואל need to teach his rule?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge against שמואל. It quotes the closing words of an earlier source that already seems to teach his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said that witnesses who swear without being asked by the plaintiff are פטור. But a known source already says witnesses are liable only when they hear the demand from the תובע himself. So שמואל's teaching looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The plaintiff, the person claiming money who needs the witnesses

phrases.english: until they hear it from the mouth of the plaintiff!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge to שמואל that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's teaching that witnesses who swear when the plaintiff only ran after them are פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier source already requires the demand to come from the plaintiff's mouth, so שמואל's rule seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Running after the witnesses is the new point
steps.stepSummary: שמואל needed to teach the case where the plaintiff ran after the witnesses. Otherwise we might think running after them counts like asking them.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל needed to teach the case where the plaintiff ran after them. You might have thought that since he is running after them, it is as if he told them to testify. So שמואל teaches us that it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל's חידוש is about a plaintiff who runs after the witnesses but says nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source only shows that some demand from the plaintiff is needed. When the plaintiff chases the witnesses, his intent is obvious, so we might treat it like a spoken demand. שמואל teaches that it is still not enough. The witnesses stay פטור unless he actually asks them.

keyTerms.meaning: Ran after them, chasing the witnesses
It was necessary for him to teach
You might have thought (the הוה אמינא)
It is like someone who said it
He teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: The case of running after them was necessary for him;
it would enter your mind to say:
since he is running after them,
it is like one who said to them to testify;
he teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new case (חידוש) that the earlier source did not clearly cover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Chasing the witnesses shows such clear intent that it counts like a spoken demand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when he chases them, the witnesses are פטור unless the plaintiff actually tells them to testify.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a clear line for שבועת העדות: obvious intent is not enough, and the demand must actually be made.

steps.title: The משנה also says the plaintiff 'said'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the משנה of שבועת העדות opens with 'he said to the witnesses, come testify for me'. That implies only an actual statement creates liability, which is שמואל's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we also learned this in the משנה: How does שבועת העדות work? The plaintiff said to witnesses, 'Come and testify for me', and they said 'We swear…' etc. So if he said it, yes, they are liable. If he did not say it, no, they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to שמואל. Even his running case seems to come straight out of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the case as one where the plaintiff 'said' to the witnesses. Reading it closely, only a spoken demand creates liability, so running after them alone would not. That means שמואל's חידוש from step 2 is already in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But we also learned this already (in a משנה)
The oath of testimony: witnesses falsely swear they know no testimony
How so? What is the case?
Yes … no (a דיוק: this case yes, otherwise no)

phrases.english: But this too we learned:
The oath of testimony, how does it work?
He said to witnesses, 'Come and testify for me,'
and they said 'An oath…' etc.
phrases.notes: כּוּ׳ means 'and so on'. Only the opening words of the משנה matter here.

phrases.english: If he said it, yes, they are liable; if he did not say it, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by showing the running case may already follow from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that the running case is a new teaching of שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'he said', which implies a spoken demand is required. So silently chasing the witnesses would already be excluded, and שמואל adds nothing.

steps.title: The word 'said' in the משנה is not exact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'said' in the משנה is not meant strictly, so we cannot learn from it that a spoken demand is needed. That is why שמואל had to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He said' is not meant exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns away the proof from the משנה. Its word 'said' is just a normal way of describing the case, not a precise requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'said' is not exact, the משנה could hold that any clear request, even without words, creates liability. So the משנה does not settle the running case. שמואל's teaching that the plaintiff must actually ask is still needed.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a plaintiff who only runs after the witnesses has not made a demand, so they are פטור if they swear falsely. The משנה's word 'said' could not prove this, because 'said' there is לאו דוקא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'לאו דוקא' to mean the גמרא rejects שמואל. It only means the משנה's wording cannot prove שמואל's rule. That is exactly why שמואל needed to say it himself.

phrases.english: 'He said' is not meant exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside the proof from the משנה raised in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference from the משנה's word 'said', not the משנה's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge treated 'said' as a strict condition, but the משנה used it loosely to describe the usual case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's teaching stands as a real חידוש. Chasing the witnesses is not a demand, and the משנה's wording did not already teach this.

steps.title: Proof from the deposit case that 'said' is not strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports step 4's claim that 'said' is not strict. In the parallel משנה about שבועת הפקדון, the same word 'said' appears, yet there it cannot be strict, because the פסוק makes the bailee liable for any kind of denial.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you don't agree that 'said' is not strict, look at the deposit case. The משנה there says: 'What is שבועת הפקדון? He said to him, give me my deposit that you are holding.' Would we really say that only if he said it is the bailee liable, and if he did not say it he is not? But the פסוק says 'and he denies to his fellow', which covers any denial at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for its claim that the word 'said' in the משנה is not meant strictly. It points to another משנה that uses the same word in a case where it clearly cannot be strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה of שבועת הפקדון also opens with 'he said to him'. But the פסוק 'וְכִחֶשׁ בַּעֲמִיתוֹ' makes the bailee liable for any false denial, whether or not there was a spoken demand. So 'said' in that משנה must just be a figure of speech, and the same word in the משנה of שבועת העדות can be read the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit: an item left with someone for safekeeping
A false oath denying that one holds someone else's deposit
'And he denies to his fellow' (the פסוק about denying a deposit)
Any amount, any kind at all
For if you do not say so (introduces a proof)

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
phrases.notes: 'So' points back to step 4: the word 'said' in the משנה isn't meant strictly.

phrases.english: regarding a deposit, where the משנה teaches:
The oath on a deposit, how is it?
He said to him: "Give me the deposit
that I have in your hand"

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי – אָמַר אִין, לָא אָמַר לָא?!
phrases.english: Here too, would we say: if he said it, yes; if he did not say it, no?!
But "and he denies to his fellow" means any denial at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings proof for step 4's claim that 'said' in the משנה is not strict.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the word 'אָמַר' in the משנה of שבועת העדות is not meant strictly
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of שבועת הפקדון, which also uses 'אָמַר', together with the פסוק 'וְכִחֶשׁ בַּעֲמִיתוֹ', which makes any denial count

steps.title: So 'said' is not strict in either משנה
steps.stepSummary: From the deposit case, the גמרא concludes that 'said' is not strict there, and so it is not strict in the משנה of שבועת העדות either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'said' there is not strict. Here too, it is not strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof: since 'said' in the deposit משנה is not strict, 'said' in the witnesses' משנה is not strict either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the proof from step 5. If the word is loose in one משנה, we cannot rely on it to be strict in the matching משנה. So the משנה of שבועת העדות does not teach that the demand must be spoken, and שמואל is needed.

phrases.english: Rather, "said" is not meant strictly;
here too, it is not meant strictly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof begun in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word 'אָמַר' is not strict in either the deposit משנה or the witnesses' משנה, so neither proves that a spoken demand is required.

steps.title: Why say 'said' twice if it is never strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison. If 'said' were strict in the witnesses' case, we could explain that the deposit משנה just copied the same wording. But if it is strict in neither, why does the משנה bother writing 'said' in both places?
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this? It would make sense if you said 'said' here, by the witnesses, is strict, and the משנה used the same word there, by the deposit, only to match. But if you say 'said' is not strict there and not strict here, why do I need the משנה to write 'said' in both places?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from steps 5 and 6. It argues that the deposit case does not show that 'said' is loose by the witnesses as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is another way to read the two משניות: 'said' is strict by the witnesses, and the משנה wrote 'said' by the deposit only to keep the wording the same. That would explain why the word appears in both places. But if the word is strict in neither place, there seems to be no reason to write it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (how can you compare these?)
Why do I need it to be taught?

phrases.english: What is this comparison?
It would be fine if you say
that "said" here is meant strictly:
phrases.notes: In this step, 'here' is the witnesses' oath and 'there' is the deposit oath.

phrases.english: he taught it there because of here.
phrases.notes: He means the משנה used 'said' for the deposit just to match the wording it used for the witnesses.

phrases.english: But if you say
that "said" there is not meant strictly
and "said" here is not meant strictly either,
why do I need it to teach "said," "said"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from the deposit case in steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that 'אָמַר' is not strict in the witnesses' משנה, based on the deposit משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading 'said' as strict by the witnesses and copied by the deposit explains why the word appears in both places. Reading it as loose in both leaves the repeated word with no purpose, so the משנה of שבועת העדות may be strict after all, and then שמואל would add nothing.

steps.title: The משנה just describes what usually happens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה says 'said' because that is the normal way people make a demand. So the word does not prove that only a spoken demand counts, and שמואל's teaching is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is just teaching us the usual way things happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the משנה writes 'said' in both places only because people usually make their demands out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating 'said' does not have to teach a law; it can simply describe the typical case. So the משנה leaves open whether a demand made without words, like running after the witnesses, also makes them liable. שמואל had to teach that it does not.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אָמַר' in the משנה describes the usual case, not a strict requirement. Since the משנה proves nothing about a demand made without words, שמואל needed to teach that only a spoken demand from the plaintiff makes the witnesses liable.

phrases.english: Perhaps the usual way of the matter
is what it is teaching us.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אוֹרְחָא דְּמִילְּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and keeps step 4's answer in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording: the repeated word describes the usual case and does not set a law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing 'said' twice must teach something, so the witnesses' משנה must require a spoken demand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה uses 'said' only because demands are usually spoken. It proves nothing, so שמואל's teaching is necessary.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that witnesses who swear 'we know no testimony for you' before anyone asked them are exempt. A bailee who denies a deposit is liable even in that situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports שמואל: The witnesses saw a man following them. They said to him, 'Why are you following us? We swear we know no testimony for you.' They are exempt. But if it was about a deposit, they are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up שמואל's rule. Witnesses are only liable for a false oath if the person actually asked them to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the man only followed the witnesses. He never actually asked them, so their oath does not make them liable. With a deposit the rule is different, because any denial at all makes the bailee liable. This is the same difference we saw in steps 5 and 6.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him (a support)
A deposit left with a bailee

steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the discussion about שמואל with a clear source on his side. Being followed is not the same as being asked.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with שמואל:
They saw him coming after them,
they said to him: "Why are you coming after us?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין לָךְ עֵדוּת״ – פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.english: We swear that we do not know any testimony for you" – they are exempt.
And if it is about a deposit – they are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 showed that שמואל's teaching was still needed, this step brings a ברייתא that supports it.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that witnesses are liable only if they were actually asked to testify
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: witnesses who swear without being asked are exempt, while a bailee is liable for any denial

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about five oaths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Someone made the witnesses swear five times.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he made them swear five times, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the witnesses were made to swear five times outside בית דין and then admitted in בית דין, they are exempt. If they denied in בית דין too, they are liable for each oath. So the משנה assumes that what really counts is the denial in בית דין.

phrases.english: If he made them swear five times, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: if they admitted in בית דין they are exempt, and if they denied there they are liable for each oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion about שמואל is finished. The גמרא now moves on to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses' liability depends on whether they deny in בית דין.

steps.title: Why only a denial in בית דין counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that witnesses are liable only for denying in בית דין, and not for denying outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that they are liable only for denying in בית דין, and not for denying outside בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule behind the משנה. Only a denial in בית דין makes the witnesses liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about שבועת העדות does not mention בית דין at all. So the גמרא wants to know where this limit comes from.

phrases.english: From where do we know
that it is for denial in בית דין that they are liable,
and for denial outside בית דין they are not liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן דְּאַכְּפִירָה בְּבֵית דִּין הוּא דִּמְחַיְּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks for the source of the rule that the משנה quoted in step 10 assumes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that only a denial in בית דין makes the witnesses liable

steps.title: אביי: only where testimony would make someone pay
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the פסוק 'if he does not tell' that the witness is liable only where his testimony would make someone pay money. That means in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, 'If he does not tell, he shall bear his sin.' I told you this only in a place where, if this one would tell, that one would become liable to pay money.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 11 using the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'if he does not tell' mean telling that actually makes a difference. That is testimony that would make the other person pay money. Outside בית דין, testimony does not make anyone pay, so denying there does not make the witnesses liable.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses become liable in שבועת העדות only by denying in בית דין. Only there would their testimony make someone pay.

phrases.english: אביי said: The verse says:
"If he does not tell, he shall bear his sin" –
I only told you this
in a place where, if this one would tell,
that one would become liable to pay money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question of step 11 from the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'if he does not tell' mean testimony that would make someone pay, and that only happens in בית דין.

steps.title: Maybe the oath itself must be in court too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: if the denial must be in בית דין, maybe the oath must also be taken in בית דין to count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, say that the oath itself must be in court to count, and an oath not in court does not count!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on אביי's last teaching. He says the same reasoning could mean the oath itself only counts in בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learned from 'if he does not tell' that the denial only matters in בית דין, where testimony brings payment. רב פפא asks why we should stop at the denial. Perhaps the oath also needs to be in בית דין for the witness to be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your reasoning is correct

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
If so, say that the oath itself —
in court, yes, it counts,
and not in court, no, it does not count!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's derivation by stretching it to the oath itself
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that only the denial has to be in בית דין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק limits liability to a place where testimony brings payment, the oath may need to be in בית דין too.

steps.title: A ברייתא makes a person liable for each oath
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the idea and brings a ברייתא: the word 'of any one' teaches liability for each and every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because a ברייתא teaches: 'of any one' means he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins his answer. He cites a ברייתא that he will use in the next step to show the oath does not need to be in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a person can owe a separate קרבן for each oath. אביי will use this as the key piece of his proof. By itself it only sets up the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind: don't think that

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as it is taught: "of any one" —
comes to make him liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts אביי's defense against רב פפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a ברייתא that liability can repeat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath must be in בית דין
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability can come separately for each oath, which will show the oath can be outside בית דין

steps.title: Five oaths in court bring only one liability
steps.stepSummary: If the oath had to be in court, the ברייתא could never apply. The משנה teaches that five oaths in בית דין bring only one liability, because a denial in court cannot be taken back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the oath must be in court, could he ever be liable for each one? We learned: if he made them swear five times before the court and they denied, they are liable only once. רבי שמעון said: Why? Since they cannot go back and admit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows that רב פפא's idea clashes with the ברייתא. In בית דין, only the first denial counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once witnesses deny in court, that denial is final and they cannot change it. So any more oaths in court add nothing, and they are liable only once. If oaths only counted in court, the ברייתא's 'liable for each one' would never happen.

phrases.english: And if you think the oath must be in court,

phrases.aramaic: מִי מְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת?!
phrases.english: would he ever be liable for each and every one?!
But didn't we learn: if he made them swear

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְכָפְרוּ –
phrases.english: five times before the court, and they denied —
they are liable only once.
Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Since they cannot go back and admit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּבֵית דִּין, מִי מְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא together with the משנה to knock down רב פפא's suggestion
steps.raayaObject: That the oath does not have to be taken in בית דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'of any one' combined with the משנה of five oaths in court

steps.title: Oath outside court, denial in court
steps.stepSummary: So the oath can be outside בית דין, but the denial must be in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this: the oath can be outside court, and the denial must be in court?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sums up his answer to רב פפא. The oath and the denial follow different rules about place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for each oath can only happen when the oaths are taken outside court. The denial still has to be in בית דין, as learned from 'if he does not tell'. This keeps both the ברייתא and the משנה true.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from it?

steps.whatToRemember: For שבועת העדות: the oath can be taken anywhere, but the witnesses are only liable if their denial happens in בית דין.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it:
the oath can be outside court,
but the denial must be in court?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The oath may be outside בית דין; the denial must be in בית דין.

steps.title: The משנה: both witnesses denied together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if both witnesses denied together, both are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both of them denied together, they are both liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that two witnesses who deny at the same moment are both liable. This is a new topic. It sets up the question in the next step about whether two things can truly happen at the same time.

phrases.english: If both of them denied together —
they are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses who deny at the same moment are both liable.

steps.title: Can two things happen at the exact same instant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: it is impossible to time two events exactly, so one denial must have come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it impossible to time things exactly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's case. Two people can never speak at exactly the same instant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one witness always denies a moment before the other, there is no real case of 'together'. Then the משנה's ruling that both are liable seems to describe something that cannot happen.

keyTerms.meaning: To time exactly, to make two things happen at precisely the same moment

phrases.english: But isn't it impossible to time things exactly?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה line just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of two witnesses denying together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exact timing is impossible, so 'together' cannot really happen.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that this משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that exact timing is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says exact timing is possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He says this משנה follows a תנא who holds that two things can happen at the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that exact timing is impossible. רב חסדא points out that רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees. So the משנה is written according to his view, and its case is real.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to time things exactly

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case of 'both denied together' follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that two events can happen at exactly the same moment.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who says it is possible to time things exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about exact timing
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exact timing is impossible, so the משנה's case cannot happen
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds exact timing is possible

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Denials close together count as together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can even follow the רבנן: the two witnesses denied within תוך כדי דיבור, which counts as one moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even if you say the משנה follows the רבנן, it is talking about a case where both witnesses denied within the short time it takes to speak a few words, and that short time counts as if it were the same speech.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer from רב חסדא to the question of how two witnesses can deny at exactly the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that exact timing is possible. רבי יוחנן says we do not need that. Even the רבנן agree that words said within תוך כדי דיבור are treated as one statement, so two denials that close together count as simultaneous.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say it follows the רבנן (the majority view)
Within the short time it takes to say a brief phrase
Is treated like the speech itself (counts as one statement)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of תוך כדי דיבור, that a short gap does not break speech, shows up all over ש״ס, for retracting statements and joining statements together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,
for example, where both of them denied
within the time of speaking a short phrase
and within the time of speaking is like the speech itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 18, in place of רב חסדא's answer in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so that the משנה fits even the majority view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, since only he holds that exact timing is possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן agree, because denials within תוך כדי דיבור count as one moment.

steps.title: The denial sentence is too long to fit
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי asks: תוך כדי דיבור is only a two- or three-word greeting, but the oath sentence is much longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of Difti said to רבינא: After all, how long is 'within the time of speaking'? The time it takes a student to greet his teacher. Some say: the time it takes a teacher to greet his student. By the time they say 'An oath that we do not know any testimony for you,' much more time has passed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges רבי יוחנן's answer by pointing out how short תוך כדי דיבור really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תוך כדי דיבור is the length of a short greeting, either three words or two words. The full oath sentence is much longer than that. So if one witness says the whole sentence and only then the other speaks, more than תוך כדי דיבור has passed, and the denials cannot count as together.

keyTerms.meaning: After all; let us think it through
A student's greeting to his teacher (שלום עליך רבי)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי תּוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר כַּמָּה הָוֵי –
phrases.english: After all, how long is 'within the time of speaking'?
The time of a student's greeting to his teacher,
phrases.notes: That greeting is three words: "שלום עליך רבי".

phrases.english: Some say:
the time of a teacher's greeting to his student;
phrases.notes: That one is even shorter, just two words: "שלום עליך".

phrases.english: by the time they say
"An oath that we do not know any testimony for you,"
it is much longer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: מִכְּדִי תּוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר כַּמָּה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the two denials happened within תוך כדי דיבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oath sentence takes far longer to say than the two- or three-word length of תוך כדי דיבור, so the second denial cannot fall within that time.

steps.title: Each witness starts right after the other finishes
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers: each witness's denial begins within תוך כדי דיבור of the end of the other's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Each one spoke within the time of speaking of his friend's statement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אחא's question by explaining how the timing is measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not need both full sentences to fit into the short time. It is enough that the second witness begins his denial within תוך כדי דיבור after the first one finishes. Then the two statements are joined and count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the speaking time after his friend's statement

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, two witnesses who deny one right after the other, with no more than a short greeting's pause, are both liable even according to the רבנן.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבינא answering רב אחא מדיפתי.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד תּוֹךְ דִּיבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: Each and every one spoke within the speaking time of his friend's statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד תּוֹךְ דִּיבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 and saves רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the time limit is measured
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both full oath sentences must fit within the short time of a greeting, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the gap between the end of one statement and the start of the next must be within תוך כדי דיבור.

steps.title: משנה: one after the other, only the first is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if the witnesses denied one after the other, the first is liable and the second is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they denied one after the other, the first is liable and the second is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a discussion about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first witness denies, only one witness is left. A single witness cannot force a payment by himself, so the second witness's denial does not cause a loss of money, and he is exempt.

phrases.english: If they denied one after the other,
the first is liable and the second is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה – הָרִאשׁוֹן חַיָּיב וְהַשֵּׁנִי פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after finishing the case of denying together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When witnesses deny one after the other, only the first is liable; the second is exempt.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה disagrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds a single witness can be liable for the oath of testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא, as it is taught in a ברייתא: If someone makes a single witness swear, the witness is exempt. But רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון holds him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out which opinion the משנה's ruling matches and which it does not, citing a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts the second witness because he is only one witness. The ברייתא's first opinion agrees that a single witness is exempt. But רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds a single witness liable, so by his view the second witness in our משנה would also be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a single witness swear

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not like this Tanna,
as it is taught:
One who makes a single witness swear, he is exempt,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא – דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which opinion the משנה line from Step 23 disagrees with.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's exemption of the second witness follows the first opinion of the ברייתא, not רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: What are the two Tannaim arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument is whether a single witness comes to bring an oath or to bring a money obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is what they argue about: One Sage holds that when a single witness comes, he comes to bring an oath. And the other Sage holds that when a single witness comes, he comes to bring money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason behind the argument in the ברייתא, setting up a discussion of whether this suggestion is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single witness cannot make someone pay, but he can force the other side to swear. The first תנא sees him as only causing an oath, so his denial causes no money loss and he is exempt. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון sees him as really about money, since the other side, if unwilling to swear, must pay, so his denial is a money denial and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is what they argue about

steps.confusionAlert: The word לימא usually signals a suggestion that the גמרא may go on to reject. Do not treat it yet as the final explanation.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is what they argue about:
that one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is the first תנא of the ברייתא, who exempts a single witness.

phrases.english: when a single witness comes,
it is for an oath that he comes;
and the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds a single witness liable.

phrases.english: when a single witness comes,
it is for money that he comes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explores the reasoning behind the ברייתא argument cited in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides the first תנא and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון about a single witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a single witness counts as causing an oath or a money obligation decides whether his false denial is a money denial, which is the key to liability for the oath of testimony.

steps.title: אביי's statement rules out the suggested explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 25 by quoting אביי, who lists the single-witness case among the cases where everyone agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really understand it that way? Didn't אביי say: All agree about a witness of a סוטה, all agree about witnesses of a סוטה, and there is a dispute about witnesses of a סוטה. All agree about one witness, and all agree about a witness whose opposing party is suspected about oaths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion from Step 25. It brings a statement of אביי that does not fit with that suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the תנאים argue about the basic nature of a single witness: does he bring an oath or bring money? But אביי puts the plain case of עד אחד on the 'everyone agrees' list. So the argument cannot be about that basic question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And can you understand it that way?' A sign the גמרא is rejecting an idea
A woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful
Suspected of swearing falsely, so he is not allowed to take an oath

steps.confusionAlert: אביי says 'witnesses of a סוטה' twice: once in an 'all agree' clause and once in a 'dispute' clause. These are two different kinds of witnesses in a סוטה case. Steps 29 and 30 explain the 'all agree' cases, and the disputed case is explained on the next amud.

phrases.english: And can you really understand it this way?!
But didn't Abaye say:
All agree regarding a witness of a sota,
and all agree regarding witnesses of a sota,
and there is a dispute regarding witnesses of a sota;
phrases.notes: Same words as the line before, but this refers to a different group of witnesses in the סוטה case.

phrases.english: all agree regarding one witness,
and all agree regarding a witness
whose opposing party is suspected about oaths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation suggested in Step 25
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the dispute is whether a single witness comes for an oath or for money
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי treats the plain single-witness case as agreed by everyone, so the dispute cannot be about the basic nature of a single witness

steps.title: New explanation: does something that causes money count as money?
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a single witness comes to bring an oath. The argument is whether something that leads to money counts as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that when a single witness comes, he comes to bring an oath. Here they disagree about this: one master holds that something that causes money is like money, and the other master holds it is not like money.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first idea, the גמרא gives a new explanation of the argument between רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree a single witness only obligates the other person to swear. But sometimes that person would rather pay than swear, so the witness indirectly causes money to be paid. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds דבר הגורם לממון counts as money, so the witness is liable. The תנא קמא holds it does not count, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' The גמרא is offering a new approach
Something that causes money to be paid, even though it is not money itself

steps.whyThisMatters: דבר הגורם לממון is a major idea that comes up in many places in ש״ס. Here it explains why a single witness might be liable for שבועת העדות even though he cannot obligate anyone to pay.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
that when one witness comes,
he comes to bring an oath;
and here they disagree about this:
One master holds that a thing that causes money
phrases.notes: This 'master' is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds the single witness is liable.

phrases.english: is considered like money,
and the other master holds it is not considered like money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about whether a single witness brings an oath or brings money
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees he brings an oath; they argue whether דבר הגורם לממון counts as money
steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation: a single witness only brings an oath, and the argument is whether 'something that causes money' counts as money.

steps.title: אביי's statement quoted in full to be explained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to אביי's statement on its own terms in order to explain each part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: אביי said: All agree about a witness of a סוטה, all agree about witnesses of a סוטה, and there is a dispute about witnesses of a סוטה. All agree about one witness, and all agree about a witness whose opposing party is suspected about oaths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אביי's statement again, this time to study it directly. This sets up the clause-by-clause explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, אביי was quoted only to reject an idea. Now the גמרא uses the word גופא to show it is turning to the statement itself, to explain what each 'all agree' and 'dispute' case means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself.' The גמרא turns to study a statement it quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself: Abaye said:
All agree regarding a witness of a sota,
and all agree regarding witnesses of a sota,
and there is a dispute regarding witnesses of a sota;
all agree regarding one witness,
and all agree regarding a witness
whose opposing party is suspected about oaths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the dispute to study אביי's statement, which was quoted in Step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי lists the witness cases where everyone agrees and the one case where there is a dispute

steps.title: A single witness to a sota's sin is liable
steps.stepSummary: The first clause of אביי means a single witness who says the סוטה sinned is liable, because the Torah believes one witness in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: All agree about a witness of a סוטה that he is liable, in the case of a witness of impurity, because the Torah believed him, as it is written: 'And there is no witness against her.' This means whatever witness there is against her is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first clause of אביי: which witness of a סוטה everyone agrees is liable, and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one witness cannot make someone pay. But for a סוטה, the פסוק teaches that even one witness who saw her sin is believed. His testimony forbids her to her husband and makes her lose her כתובה, so it really affects money. That is why everyone agrees he is liable for שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness who testifies that the סוטה actually sinned, making her forbidden to her husband
'And there is no witness against her' (במדבר ה:יג)

phrases.english: All agree regarding a witness of a sota that he is liable,
meaning a witness of impurity;
phrases.notes: He means a witness who says she actually sinned, not just that she was alone with the man.

phrases.english: because the Torah believed him,
as it is written: "And there is no witness against her" —
any witness there is against her is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד סוֹטָה שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּעֵד טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first clause of אביי's statement quoted in Step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single witness who testifies that a סוטה sinned is liable for שבועת העדות, because the Torah believes one witness in this case
steps.whyThisMatters: This is an exception to the usual rule: here a single witness's testimony has real legal and money results, so his false oath makes him liable.

steps.title: Witnesses of warning are exempt because they are only a cause of a cause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the second clause of אביי: everyone agrees that witnesses of a סוטה are exempt. This means the witnesses of warning (עדי קינוי), since their testimony is only a גורם דגורם, a cause of a cause, of money loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: And everyone agrees that witnesses of a סוטה are exempt. This means the witnesses of warning, because they are only a cause of a cause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next part of אביי's statement. It tells us which witnesses of a סוטה are exempt and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses of warning only show that the husband warned his wife. She loses her כתובה only after more steps: witnesses that she secluded herself with the man, and then a witness that she sinned or her drinking the bitter water. Since the warning is two steps away from the money loss, even someone who holds that 'a cause of money is like money' (Step 27) agrees these witnesses are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: And everyone agrees: this case is outside the argument
Witnesses that the husband warned his wife not to be alone with a certain man
A cause of a cause: something two steps away from the result
Exempt: here, not liable for the oath of testimony

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 29. There the single witness who says she sinned is liable, because his testimony directly costs her the כתובה. Here the witnesses of warning are exempt, because they are much further from the money loss.
steps.whatToRemember: How far testimony is from the money loss matters. A direct witness (that she sinned) is liable, but witnesses of warning, who are only a גורם דגורם, are exempt according to everyone.

phrases.english: And everyone agrees regarding witnesses of a סוטה that he is exempt,
this means witnesses of warning;
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who saw the husband warn his wife not to be alone with a certain man.

phrases.english: since it is a cause of a cause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line explanation of אביי's statement started in Step 28, moving from the first clause (Step 29) to the second clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses of warning of a סוטה are exempt from the oath of testimony according to everyone, since their testimony is only a cause of a cause of money loss.
